tagline: Old Safford Road keeps the bridges in service.
intro: Old Safford Road runs southwest out of Clifton as the Black Hills Back Country Byway. It crosses the Gila on a pair of concrete arches and then a short gap on a slab laced with railroad rail.

Both bridges were built by convict labor, and Black Gap was the last-completed link in the Clifton-Solomonville Highway across Greenlee and Graham counties. U.S. 666 later took most of that traffic away. The old road stayed on as a county route, and its bridges still carry local cars.

moments.title: Clifton
moments.text: The road sets out from the Greenlee County seat on the San Francisco River, a town caught up in Arizona's copper mine strike of 1983.

moments.title: Gila River Bridge
moments.text: Wartime steel was scarce and bids ran high, so the river is crossed on two equal Luten arches built in 1918, with Owl Creek Campground on the cliff above.

moments.title: Black Gap Bridge
moments.text: Railroad rails, set 24 inches apart inside the concrete, carry the road over this single short span, built in 1920 and 1921.
